goal: Create a reusable deterministic verifier for Factory package MANIFEST/hash/path integrity without duplicating Portable v2 semantic verification or approval logic.
constraints: Python standard library only for the produced artifact.
Do not claim semantic correctness, evidence sufficiency, or release approval.
Do not add a new Factory Core module.
acceptance_criteria: Valid Factory package passes integrity verification.
Hash tampering, missing/unexpected files, traversal paths, symlinks, duplicate manifest paths, malformed manifest rows, and unreadable/corrupt package members are detected.
Malformed non-object MANIFEST files[] rows fail closed with a machine-readable FAIL receipt instead of raising an uncaught exception.
CLI returns machine-readable receipt and non-zero exit on failure.
Artifact explicitly reports semantic correctness, evidence sufficiency, and release approval as NOT_ASSESSED.
Artifact tests and full Factory regression suite pass.
Coordinated payload+manifest tampering is detected when an externally frozen MANIFEST.json SHA-256 is supplied.
Required manifest scalar types reject booleans/nulls and malformed values fail closed.
NUL, C0/DEL/C1 control characters, dot-segment, repeated-slash, Windows-drive, traversal, and absolute paths are rejected without uncaught exceptions.
Unsafe ZIP directory entries are detected; safe explicit ZIP directory entries remain supported.
Unreadable directory enumeration cannot silently hide unexpected members.
Control-character and colon-bearing/ADS-like manifest paths are rejected before member verification.
